ai.description: This 4–6 cm frog has a mottled brown-grey dorsum with dark spots. It features expanded, truncate toe discs for climbing and a distinct white upper lip stripe. It inhabits fast-flowing mountain streams.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Amolops marmoratus* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, marbled or mottled pattern on its flanks and limbs, which contrasts with the more uniform coloration of other *Amolops* species.
ai.habitat: The Marbled Sucker Frog inhabits fast-flowing, rocky hill streams within evergreen or semi-evergreen forests at elevations ranging from 200 to 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Marbled Sucker Frog is primarily nocturnal, using its specialized abdominal sucker to cling firmly to wet rocks in fast-flowing mountain streams to avoid being swept away.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Amolops marmoratus* breeds in fast-flowing streams during the monsoon (June–August), laying eggs in clutches attached to submerged rocks or vegetation.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Amolops marmoratus* is found in Northeast India, specifically in Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, and Meghalaya, inhabiting streams at elevations between 200 and 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Marbled Sucker Frog produces a high-pitched, rhythmic series of short, insect-like chirps while perched on wet rocks near fast-flowing mountain streams.
